title: Quick start
description: Start a local storage API, upload your first file, and prepare to connect your Mac.

sections.title: Get the source
paragraphs: Install Bun 1.4.2 or enter the repository’s Flox environment, then install the locked dependencies.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/smeltery/loft.git
cd loft
flox activate
bun install --frozen-lockfile

sections.title: Start your storage API
paragraphs: In this terminal, choose a random token and keep its value for the client. The disk backend writes data beneath LOFT_DATA. Keep that directory between runs.
sections.code:
export LOFT_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
export LOFT_DATA="$PWD/.loft-data"
bun --filter @loft/api dev

sections.title: Verify the connection
paragraphs: In a second terminal, set LOFT_API and LOFT_TOKEN to your server address and the same token you chose above. Health is public; listing files requires the token.
sections.code:
export LOFT_API="http://127.0.0.1:8787"
export LOFT_TOKEN="<your-token>"
curl --fail "$LOFT_API/health"
curl --fail -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOFT_TOKEN" \
  "$LOFT_API/v1/files"

sections.title: Upload your first file
paragraphs: Use a stable file ID and supply a display name. This example creates a small text file in Inbox.
sections.code:
printf "Hello from loft.\n" > hello.txt
curl --fail-with-body -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOFT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  -H "X-Loft-Name: hello.txt" \
  --data-binary @hello.txt \
  "$LOFT_API/v1/files/hello/content"

sections.title: Connect a client
paragraphs: For the self-hosted web interface, start the web workspace from the repository root. Open http://localhost:3000/app and enter your token in settings.
